issues.title: Persistent USE failure (stale or dropped current keyspace) now discards every new connection and drains the pool to Broken(UseKeyspaceError)
issues.verdictReason: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace (connection_pool.rs:1287) and ClusterWorker (worker.rs:351) store the keyspace before USE succeeds and never roll it back; the new Err(Keyspace) arm drops each connection whose USE fails, so after a failed use_keyspace or a DROP KEYSPACE every refill is discarded with growing backoff, the pool drains to Broken(UseKeyspaceError) and emit_events sends ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost. Before the PR the connection was kept with a warn!, so fully qualified queries kept working.
issues.scopeReason: Direct consequence of the PR's discard-on-USE-failure change.

issues.title: USE failure on a new connection logged at debug! instead of warn!, and only surfaced via shared_conns when the pool is empty
issues.verdictReason: The removed code logged at warn!; the new arm logs at debug! while now also dropping the connection. With a non-empty pool update_shared_conns is not called, so a pool that can never grow is invisible at default log levels.
issues.scopeReason: Log level changed by this PR's keyspace-failure arm.

issues.title: Excess shard-aware connection dropped without decrementing total_connections
issues.verdictReason: The else-if requested_shard.is_some() branch drops a connection that count_in_metrics already counted via inc_total_connections, with no dec_total_connections; the counter drifts up on every shard-aware miss (e.g. behind NAT). Branch is unchanged from base.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing, but it is the one discard site in handle_ready_connection left unbalanced by the PR's own metric-balancing commits.

issues.title: Pool teardown (run() exit / PoolRefiller drop) never decrements total_connections
issues.verdictReason: When the keyspace request channel closes, run() returns and PoolRefiller with all conns and excess_connections is dropped; there is no Drop impl or decrement, so the gauge keeps the pool's full count. full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics asserts total_connections == 1 after the worker has exited, encoding the leak.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing leak, but the PR's new metrics test bakes it in as expected behavior.

issues.title: No timeout on per-connection use_keyspace in start_setting_keyspace_for_connection; a hung USE stalls all refills
issues.verdictReason: The future pushed to ready_connections awaits connection.use_keyspace with no timeout (explicit TODO), keeping is_filling() true so need_filling() never schedules another refill; the sibling PoolRefiller::use_keyspace does wrap USE in tokio::time::timeout.
issues.scopeReason: The untimed await and its TODO exist unchanged at base; the PR does not change hang behavior.

issues.title: USE failure for a stale keyspace discards the connection instead of retrying with the current keyspace
issues.verdictReason: The Ok arm re-checks evt.keyspace_name against current_keyspace, but the Err(Keyspace) arm does not; if the keyspace changes while an old USE is in flight and that USE fails, the connection is dropped and backoff is raised. Self-heals on the next refill.
issues.scopeReason: Introduced by the new Err(Keyspace) arm.

issues.title: PR description omits the metric-balancing commits and keyspace/reshard reordering
issues.verdictReason: The PR body only describes keyspace-setup discard; commits de164845, 0d91aa54 and 617139df (metric decrements and tests) are not mentioned, nor are the warn!->debug! change or the defensible keyspace-before-reshard ordering change.

issues.title: PR validation command never compiled or ran the metrics tests or metrics assertions
issues.verdictReason: The listed command filters to keyspace_setup_failure tests without --features metrics (not a default feature), so the three #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] tests and the cfg-gated get_total_connections asserts were never exercised by it. CI does run --all-features.

issues.title: All four commits are subject-only, contrary to CONTRIBUTING.md and the ticked checklist item
issues.verdictReason: git log shows empty bodies for de164845, 0d91aa54, 7f48315d and 617139df; CONTRIBUTING.md requires messages to explain what and why, and none explains the behavior change or the keyspace/reshard reordering.

issues.title: 'Fixes: #1682' does not resolve in this repository
issues.verdictReason: gh issue view 1682 fails in dkropachev/quillstone; the number refers to upstream scylla-rust-driver, so the annotation neither links nor closes anything.

issues.title: Metric-balancing fix is bundled into the keyspace-failure PR
issues.verdictReason: Three of four commits fix total_connections accounting on pool clears, which is unrelated to the keyspace-setup issue the PR claims to fix.

issues.title: Commit 617139df is a fixup of 0d91aa54 and should be squashed
issues.verdictReason: 617139df only swaps yield_now() for a 1 ms sleep inside the test 0d91aa54 added; CONTRIBUTING.md asks for each commit to be one logically coherent change.

issues.title: Metric-balancing commit de164845 lands without tests; they come in the next commit
issues.verdictReason: de164845 adds decrement_total_connections and the decrement sites; the covering tests are only added in 0d91aa54.

issues.title: New keyspace tests do not call setup_tracing()
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill (1474) and keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state (1526) omit setup_tracing(), while every other test in the module calls it and CONTRIBUTING.md says new tests should.

issues.title: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill asserts need_filling()/is_empty() which are trivially true and do not prove a refill is scheduled
issues.verdictReason: On a fresh refiller with no conns and no pending futures, is_empty() and need_filling() hold regardless of the fix; run() is never driven, so only had_error_since_last_refill and the Broken snapshot are meaningful.

issues.title: No test drives a failing USE through run() to observe the backoff-delayed refill across cycles
issues.verdictReason: Tests only call handle_ready_connection directly; the scheduling branch in run() and on_fill_error() growth after repeated keyspace failures are covered only transitively.

issues.title: Keyspace-failure arm untested with a non-empty pool on a shard-aware attempt
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state uses requested_shard: None and does not assert had_error_since_last_refill; the requested_shard: Some case is only tested with an empty pool.

issues.title: No test covers recovery from Broken(UseKeyspaceError) back to Ready
issues.verdictReason: No test drives a pool to Broken via keyspace failure and then admits a connection whose USE succeeds.
issues.scopeReason: New Broken reason introduced by this PR.

issues.title: No test covers keyspace failure emptying the pool and emitting ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill uses no connectivity_events_sender, and preserves_pool_state keeps one connection alive, so the Lost transition is never asserted.
issues.scopeReason: New failure path introduced by this PR.

issues.title: maybe_reshard's excess_connections.len() decrement term is never exercised
issues.verdictReason: resharding_discards_old_connections_and_balances_metrics reshards with an empty excess_connections, so a miscount in that half of the sum would go unnoticed.

issues.title: Metrics tests increment total_connections manually instead of through start_opening_connection
issues.verdictReason: Every new test calls metrics.inc_total_connections() by hand before handle_ready_connection, so the real increment in count_in_metrics is never paired with the new decrements.

issues.title: decrement_total_connections loops single decrements instead of one bulk Metrics operation
issues.verdictReason: The helper calls dec_total_connections() count times (count RMWs, transient intermediate values); a dec_total_connections_by(n) on Metrics/metrics_noop would be one fetch_sub and live next to its sibling.

issues.title: dec_total_connections wraps on over-decrement instead of saturating
issues.verdictReason: fetch_sub on AtomicU64 would wrap if ever over-decremented, but no current over-decrement path exists: cleared connections cannot reach remove_connection, which only decrements when the Arc is found in conns or excess_connections.
issues.scopeReason: Metrics implementation is untouched by the PR; risk is hypothetical.

issues.title: 'Decrement then clear excess_connections' pattern duplicated across three sites
issues.verdictReason: run() (674), handle_ready_connection (1031) and maybe_reshard (1114) each pair decrement_total_connections with a clear; a clear_excess_connections() helper would keep the invariant in one place.

issues.title: Decrement sites lack a comment explaining why they cannot double count
issues.verdictReason: The decrements are correct only because dropped connections' wait_for_error futures fail to upgrade their Weak and never reach remove_connection; nothing documents this.

issues.title: Moved keyspace-setup block has no comment explaining why it must precede resharding
issues.verdictReason: The block's comment is unchanged from base and does not say that running maybe_reshard first would wipe the pool for a connection later discarded; only the test guards the ordering.

issues.title: Keyspace setup now precedes sharder/shard-aware-port update, deferring shard discovery while USE fails
issues.verdictReason: Intentional and harmless: a connection whose USE fails cannot be admitted anyway, and learning its sharder first would reshard and clear the live pool; the PR description states setup completes before resharding and a test asserts it.

issues.title: Keyspace failure on a shard-aware attempt gets no immediate regular-port retry and raises backoff
issues.verdictReason: The Connection arm's carve-out exists because the shard-aware port may be unreachable while the regular port works; a USE failure repeats on any port, so no fallback is useful and raising backoff is appropriate.

issues.title: ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError classifies a healthy-transport USE failure as a connection fault
issues.verdictReason: ConnectionError is documented as a connection-level fault, but a USE failure such as DbError::Invalid leaves the transport healthy. The new public variant therefore stretches the error's semantic contract.

issues.title: UseKeyspaceError variant message diverges from the file's existing pattern
issues.verdictReason: Other UseKeyspaceError wrappers in errors.rs (lines 80, 142, 172) use "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}".

issues.title: Private ConnectionSetupError does not document its Connection-vs-Keyspace invariant
issues.verdictReason: The enum has no documentation explaining that Keyspace means an already-counted connection that must skip shard-aware fallback, while Connection preserves the previous retry behavior.

issues.title: Err(Keyspace) with keyspace_name: None is representable though impossible in production
issues.verdictReason: OpenedConnectionEvent keeps keyspace_name separate from result, and keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill constructs exactly that combination.

issues.title: Private ConnectionSetupError duplicates ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError
issues.verdictReason: The private enum carries a distinct invariant: Keyspace errors come from an already-counted connection and must skip the shard-aware fallback, which folding into ConnectionError would lose.

issues.title: Keyspace-failure test never uses requested_shard
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill explicitly constructs requested_shard: Some(Shard(0)) at lines 1502-1506, so the claim that no test covers a requested shard is incorrect.

issues.title: Keyspace arm calls dec_total_connections inline instead of decrement_total_connections
issues.verdictReason: A single decrement calling dec_total_connections() directly matches remove_connection (1232); the helper is for counts.

issues.title: Tests re-implement OPTIONS/STARTUP proxy rules instead of reusing start_simulated_node
issues.verdictReason: make_rules (1528) and the two literal rule sets in the resharding test restate start_simulated_node's rules; a handshake change needs edits in several places.

issues.title: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill hand-builds PoolRefiller instead of mock_pool_refiller()
issues.verdictReason: The constructor call duplicates mock_pool_refiller(); the test could use it and read the metrics and pool_updated_notify fields.

issues.title: unrequested_connection_event duplicates shard_aware_attempt_result
issues.verdictReason: Same body except requested_shard; generalizing the existing helper would remove it.

issues.title: Hand-encoded SET_KEYSPACE RESULT bytes in test are undocumented and silently desync-prone
issues.verdictReason: b"\0\0\0\x03\0\x08keyspace" (kind 3, short length 8, name) has no comment and must track the keyspace name and RESULT parsing by hand.

issues.title: Test uses ShardInfo::new(...) where sibling tests use struct literals
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state builds ShardInfo via ::new while the other tests use literals.

issues.title: initial_shard_info passed to start_simulated_node is immediately overridden in resharding test
issues.verdictReason: change_request_rules replaces SUPPORTED with a non-sharded response right after start_simulated_node(initial_shard_info), so the argument has no effect.

issues.title: Inconsistent proxy.finish() handling; new metrics tests discard proxy errors with let _
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state matches the result (1689) while the new metrics tests (1939, 1967, 2012) use let _ like pre-existing tests, hiding rule/frame failures.

issues.title: full_pool metrics test polls the counter with 1 ms sleeps instead of a deterministic wait
issues.verdictReason: The awaited state is reached after one synchronous handle_ready_connection with a 5 s timeout, so it is not load-sensitive; pool_updated_notify is not signaled on the excess-clear path, so it is no alternative.

issues.title: Commit subject 'avoid busy-waiting' overstates a change that still polls
issues.verdictReason: Replacing a yield_now() spin with sleep(1ms) does stop busy-waiting; periodic sleeping is polling, not busy-waiting.

issues.title: New public ConnectionError variant has no changelog entry
issues.verdictReason: The repository has no changelog file; the variant carries a doc comment and the enum is #[non_exhaustive].

issues.title: Pool-full excess clear in run() has no test
issues.verdictReason: full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics spawns run() and asserts that exact decrement.

issues.title: #[from] publishes an unnecessary From<UseKeyspaceError> for ConnectionError conversion
issues.verdictReason: The transparent #[from] attribute adds a public conversion even though only one in-crate site needs to wrap the error; an explicit conversion there would avoid expanding the public API.

issues.title: Private ConnectionSetupError lacks Debug
issues.verdictReason: The new private enum does not derive Debug, forcing tests to manually match variants instead of using ordinary assertion diagnostics.

issues.title: ConnectionSetupError is confusingly close to the public ConnectionSetupRequestError it wraps
issues.verdictReason: The private enum's name differs by only 'Request' from errors::ConnectionSetupRequestError, even though it represents the broader post-open connection-or-keyspace outcome.
